target.title: fix(browser): remote-CDP focus emulation + early /c/ URL persistence for recoverable runs
target.body:
Addresses the remote-CDP half of #284: remote runs that die mid-wait leave unrecoverable metadata, and — as it turns out — remote sends can silently fail in the first place when the target window is backgrounded.

## Two gaps, one scenario

Remote-CDP ChatGPT targets typically live in background or occluded windows (headless servers, minimized Chrome). Live-testing against an **offscreen Chrome 149 window** surfaced both problems:

**1. ChatGPT drops the synthetic send click when the window isn't focused/visible.**
The click is logged, but the prompt never leaves the composer. The `commitProbe` diagnostics from #288 captured it precisely:

```
{"userMatched":false, "hasNewTurn":false, "stopVisible":false,
 "composerCleared":false, "editorLength":153, "turnsCount":0, "href":"https://chatgpt.com/"}
```

Full prompt still in the composer, zero turns — the send never happened. Local mode never hits this because the launched window is naturally frontmost. Fix: enable `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled` after connect (the same approach Puppeteer/Playwright use for background targets), so the page behaves like a foreground tab.

**2. Remote mode never persists the `/c/<id>` URL until the response completes.**
The local path has a background conversation-hint loop (`scheduleConversationHint("post-submit", ...)`); the remote path only re-reads the URL immediately before assistant wait/recheck. A remote run killed mid-wait by an external watchdog leaves `tabUrl: "https://chatgpt.com/"` in metadata — `resolveSessionTabRef`/`recoverConversationTab` then have nothing to recover by, which is the stale-target reattach failure described in #284. Fix: port the hint loop to the remote path via a shared, testable poller (`pollConversationUrl`), stopped in `finally` so it can't outlive the run.

## Live A/B (offscreen Chrome 149 window, remote CDP, macOS, signed-in profile)

| | send | `/c/` URL in session metadata | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| without focus emulation | silently dropped | root URL only | `prompt-commit-timeout`, prompt stuck in composer |
| with this PR | commits | persisted seconds after submit, while the answer was still generating (2m03s run) | full 876-token answer captured |

The post-submit hint fired immediately after send:

```
Clicked send button
[browser] conversation url (post-submit) = https://chatgpt.com/c/6a47c140-...
```

and the completed session metadata carries `tabUrl`/`conversationId`/`promptSubmitted` for recovery.

Harness note: "remote" Chrome was a locally launched instance with `--remote-debugging-port` and a copied signed-in profile, window positioned offscreen to match the background-window conditions of real remote servers. Two additional runs hit ChatGPT session-token rotation from sharing the profile with a live Chrome — harness noise, excluded from the A/B (their failures showed a login redirect in `commitProbe`, not the click drop).

## Changes

- `runRemoteBrowserMode`: enable focus emulation after domain enablers (soft-fails with a log line if the target rejects it).
- New module-level `pollConversationUrl` helper + `pollConversationUrlForTest` export; remote path schedules it post-submit with the same label/timeout semantics as local mode, guarded by a stop flag set in `finally` and on connection loss.
- Tests: 4 new unit tests for the poller (URL appears after polls, resilient to read errors, stop flag, root URL rejected).

## Checks

- `pnpm run check` clean
- `pnpm vitest run` — 1393 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed
- Live remote-CDP smokes above ran against this branch (no "Answer now" clicks; conversations archived per default)
